Q2FY27 FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE
- Revenue ₹2,391 Cr, up 61% YoY and 18.8% QoQ

- Gross Margin 9.6%, expanding 133 bps YoY

- Reported PAT ₹129 Cr, up 93% YoY

H1FY27 FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE
- Revenue ₹4,403 Cr, up 68% YoY
- EBITDA ₹346 Cr
- PAT ₹234 Cr, up 112% YoY
- Operating Cash Flow ₹136 Cr
- Previous year's operating cash flow: ₹101 Cr outflow

BUSINESS AND PRODUCT MIX
- Advanced Gold contributed 16% of Q2 business
- Exceeded FY27 target of 15%
- Advanced Gold contributed approximately 120 bps gross margin
- Natural and lab-grown diamond jewellery contributed 2.5-2.6% revenue
- Focus on higher-margin studded and diamond jewellery
- Lightweight jewellery is 20-30% lighter
- Technology-led manufacturing supports lightweight products

EXPORTS AND INTERNATIONAL EXPANSION
- Q2 exports reached ₹435 Cr
- FY23 full-year exports were ₹35 Cr
- Exports now contribute approximately 18% of business
- Annualised export run rate approximately ₹1,600 Cr
- Dubai office supports expansion across GCC markets
- Expanding presence across Singapore and Malaysia
- Targeting Saudi Arabia, UK and Japan

WORKING CAPITAL AND DEBT
- Net working capital reduced to 55 days
- Previous working capital cycle: 63 days
- Net debt stood at ₹531 Cr
- March 2026 net debt: ₹550 Cr
- H1 operating cash flow conversion reached 58% of PAT
- Net interest cost declined to 0.89% of sales
- Previous net interest cost: 0.96%
- Receivable days stood at 33
- Festive receivables expected during October-November

ACQUISITIONS AND GROWTH STRATEGY
- Acquisitions target additional product categories
- Focus on management expertise and customer relationships
- Rishabh Gold Mangalsutra volumes reached 150 kg monthly
- Previous monthly volumes were 20-25 kg
- Rishabh Gold revenue increased to ₹175 Cr
- Previous revenue stood at ₹49 Cr
- Rishabh Gold profit increased to ₹18.8 Cr
- Previous profit stood at ₹1.6 Cr
- Management sees further industry consolidation opportunities

FUNDRAISING AND LAND MONETISATION
- Management discussed proposed ₹1,800 Cr fundraise
- Utilisation details remain undisclosed due to regulatory restrictions
- Land monetisation reached advanced due-diligence stage
- Prospective buyer discussions remain underway
- Promoters may acquire land without commitment
- Decision expected within 20-30 days

MANAGEMENT COMMENTARY
- No fresh forward guidance due to SEBI restrictions
- Historical PAT margin guidance remains 5-5.25%
- Management reiterated guidance remains on track
- Focus on exports and advanced gold products
- Priorities include margins and capital efficiency
- Operating cash flow remains a key priority
- Promoters linked salaries to operating cash flow generation

KEY TAKEAWAYS
- Strong revenue and profitability growth continued
- Advanced Gold exceeded its FY27 contribution target
- Export business reached 18% revenue contribution
- Operating cash flow turned positive during H1
- Working capital cycle improved to 55 days
- Debt declined compared with March 2026
- Rishabh Gold acquisition delivered significant growth
- Proposed ₹1,800 Cr fundraise requires monitoring
- Land monetisation remains subject to final commitment
- Track cash conversion, margins and debt levels

ESHA MEDIA : SIGNS AI PLATFORM AGREEMENT WORTH RS 1.26 CR PER PHASE

• Company entered into a platform design, development, deployment and maintenance agreement with LivingAI Solution LLP
• Platform is an AI-powered enterprise-grade media intelligence, reputation management and actionable feedback system
• Development of various modules in phases for ₹1.26 Cr for each phase, exclusive of applicable taxes
• Agreement tenure is one year, with maintenance of services on mutually agreed terms
• Domestic agreement, in the normal course of business; no related-party transaction and no promoter or group interest in the counterparty
Impact: Positive (Adds an AI-driven media intelligence platform capability, though total contract value depends on the number of phases)

OMAXE : INCORPORATES WHOLLY OWNED SUBSIDIARY OMAXE LUCKNOW BUS TERMINAL

• Wholly owned subsidiary incorporated on October 30, 2026.
• Omaxe subscribed 10,000 equity shares for ₹1 lakh, representing 100%.
Impact: No material financial impact disclosed.

SHYAMMETL : APPROVES RS 360 CR CAPEX FOR PHUTAMURA COAL BLOCK

• Board approved 51% controlling equity stake acquisition in Alom Solar Private Limited, subject to definitive agreements and approvals
• Alom Solar holds mining rights for Phutamura Coal Block across ~7.324 sq km with estimated reserves of ~170 million tonnes
• Acquisition cost ₹0.51 L in cash for 5,100 equity shares; Alom Solar will become a subsidiary
• Initial capex budget approximately ₹360 Cr; company's 51% contribution ~₹183.60 Cr, balance by JV partner
• Completion expected on or before 30 November 2026; strategic backward integration to secure long-term coal supply for captive power and steel operations
Impact: Positive (51% acquisition of coal block entity and ₹360 Cr capex support long-term captive coal supply)

APCOTEXIND : ACQUIRES 1.275% STAKE IN AMPLUS AMPERE FOR RS 72 L

• Apcotex completed acquisition of 7,20,000 equity shares (1.275%) of Amplus Ampere Private Limited from NRB Bearings
• Cash consideration for the stake was ₹72 L; acquisition completed on 31 October 2026
• Amplus Ampere is a subsidiary of Amplus Energy Solutions PTE Ltd and operates as an SPV in the power sector
• Objective is captive consumption of solar power generated by Amplus Ampere
• Amplus Ampere reported FY25-26 turnover of ₹17.25 Cr
Impact: Positive (Adds captive solar power access for Apcotex through a small cash outlay)

KESAR ENTERPRISES : BAHERI SUGAR UNDERTAKING SALE MOU TERMINATED

• MoU dated 8 September 2026 with Avadh Foods and Multi Warehouse Private Limited for sale of Baheri sugar undertaking (Bareilly, UP) terminated
• Termination under Clause 21(c) effective 31 October 2026 as buyer failed to make payments within stipulated time and did not cure defaults despite notice
• Proposed slump sale will not proceed; the undertaking continues to be owned by the company
• Company to initiate appropriate legal action against the buyer for remedies under the MoU and in law
• Company will continue to evaluate options for the undertaking; material developments to be disclosed
Impact: Negative (Buyer default halts planned slump sale, deferring expected sale proceeds while the undertaking stays on the books)

• Completion period approx. 8 months, with 10% advance

• No promoter/promoter group interest in the awarding entity; not a related party transaction
Impact: Positive (Adds executable PEB order book in the aviation-infrastructure segment with a defined 8-month delivery timeline)

SUN PHARMA – Q2 FY27 CONCALL HIGHLIGHTS

💊 KEY PRODUCT & PIPELINE UPDATES

• Illumia faced a slowdown in the US due to market and execution factors. Received US approval for psoriatic arthritis; soft launch planned for November.

• ONLOXIT received preferred recommendation in NCCN guidelines. New long-term data showed efficacy and tolerability.

• Launched 5 new generic products in the US during Q2.

• Partnership with Leap Therapeutics for Liraglutide to expand the innovative portfolio for cholesterol management outside the US and China.

• Generic Semaglutide launched by a partner in Brazil. Already commercialised in India and South Africa.

• Launched 15 new products in India during Q2.

🔬 R&D AND INNOVATION

• Q2 R&D Spend: ₹778 Cr, representing 4.8% of sales.

• Innovative R&D accounted for 32.4% of total R&D expenditure.

• Management expects R&D spending to increase significantly in H2 FY27.

RELIANCE INDUSTRIES Q2 FY27: O2C REVENUE SURGES 44.2% TO ₹2.32 LAKH CR; EBITDA JUMPS 67.9% ON STRONG REFINING MARGINS

• Segment Revenue: Oil-to-Chemicals (O2C) revenue surged 44.2% YoY to ₹2,31,601 Cr, driven by higher energy prices and improved downstream chemical realizations

• Segment EBITDA: Jumped 67.9% YoY to ₹25,203 Cr, supported by strong transportation fuel cracks and improved downstream chemical margins

• Crude Oil Prices: Crude oil prices increased 40.6% YoY amid Middle East supply disruptions

• Transportation Fuel Prices: Increased 50–78% YoY, supported by global supply shortages and refining disruptions

• Chemical Prices: Most downstream chemical product prices increased 25–35% YoY, supporting revenue growth

• Refining Margins: Fuel cracks surged 3–3.7x YoY and reached historic highs during the quarter

• Polyester Margins: Polyester chain margins recovered sharply to a three-year high, led by PX and PTA spreads

• Global Oil Demand: Increased by 3.4 million barrels per day YoY to 102.5 million barrels per day

• Brent Crude: Averaged $97 per barrel, up 40.6% YoY, due to geopolitical disruptions and tightening global crude supplies

• Global Refinery Supply: Refinery crude throughput declined by 3.5 million barrels per day YoY to 80.9 million barrels per day

• Gasoline Margins: Singapore gasoline cracks surged 196% to $24.9 per barrel amid tightening inventories and supply disruptions

• Diesel Margins: Gasoil cracks jumped 252% to $65.8 per barrel, supported by refinery outages and global supply constraints

• Polymer Demand: Domestic polymer demand declined 3.5% YoY due to higher prices, limited availability and seasonal weakness

• Polyester Demand: Domestic polyester demand declined 6.1% YoY amid price volatility and cautious purchasing

• PET Demand: Grew 5.3% YoY, supported by healthy beverage-sector demand

• Profitability Constraints: Earnings growth was partially offset by continued SAED-related costs and under-recoveries in the Jio-bp business

• Business Outlook: Strong refining cracks, improved chemical spreads and global supply disruptions supported O2C profitability, while domestic demand weakness and elevated input costs remained key challenges

• H2 FY27 Pricing Outlook: Management does not expect significant additional discounts or major pricing reductions for mutual fund RTA services during H2 FY27.

• FY28 AMC Contract Renewals: Management indicated that contracts with some large AMCs will come up for renewal next year, with the financial impact yet to be determined.

• EBITDA Margin Outlook: Management expects consolidated EBITDA margins to expand approximately 100–200 bps annually under normal business conditions, supported by operating leverage and productivity improvements.

• Operating Expense Guidance: Management aims to keep annual operating expense growth below 10%, supported by automation, workforce optimization and technology-led efficiencies.

• MF AUM Performance: CAMS-serviced mutual fund average AUM increased approximately 12.5% YoY to ₹58.5 lakh Cr, with market share around 67%.

• Equity MF AUM: Equity average AUM increased 15.5% YoY, compared with industry growth of 15.2%.

• SIP Collections: Gross SIP collections increased 16.5% YoY during Q2, compared with industry growth of 12.4%.

• Equity Net Sales: CAMS-serviced AMCs accounted for more than 70% of industry equity net sales over the preceding year.

• AMC Client Expansion: InCred AMC appointed CAMS as its mutual fund RTA, taking the customer base to 32 out of 64 licensed AMCs.

• New AMC Launches: ASK Investments and Carnelian commenced their maiden funds during Q2, while Oaklane and Neo are expected to go live during Q3 FY27.

• Specialized Investment Funds: Approximately 12 CAMS-serviced AMCs have launched SIFs, with combined AUM around ₹20,000 Cr and an investor base approaching 1 lakh.

• SIF Pricing Outlook: Management indicated that SIF servicing yields will broadly match the corresponding regular mutual fund categories.

• GIFT City Business: Retail fund AUM crossed ₹1,500 Cr, with another 2–3 fund launches expected during Q3 FY27.

• CAMSPay Performance: Revenue increased more than 50% YoY and 13% QoQ, with the business contributing over 6% of consolidated revenue.

• CAMSPay Business Expansion: Growth is being driven by NACH, eNACH, UPI AutoPay and the expanding payment gateway and cards business.

• KRA Growth Outlook: Management expects continued growth through increasing brokerage-sector penetration, new client acquisitions and higher transaction volumes.

• KRA Customer Expansion: Five of India's top 10 brokerage houses are now active CAMS KRA clients.

• Fee Income Outlook: Management expects non-interest income to remain around 0.95–1% of assets, with NIM expansion and operating cost efficiencies contributing more significantly to ROA improvement.
• Insurance Commission Regulations: Management is evaluating alternative fee income opportunities in response to proposed regulatory changes, but expects the overall profitability impact to be manageable.
• Q2 Advances: Gross advances increased 23.4% YoY and 7.5% QoQ to ₹9,755 Cr.
• Q2 Disbursements: Loan disbursements increased 36% YoY to ₹1,095 Cr.
• Q2 Deposits: Total deposits increased 16.2% YoY to ₹10,831 Cr, while CASA deposits stood at ₹3,734 Cr, representing approximately 34.5% of deposits.
• Cost of Deposits: Cost of deposits declined to 5.68% from 5.92% YoY, supporting net interest margins.
• Q2 NII: Net interest income increased 24% YoY to ₹139 Cr from ₹112 Cr.
• Q2 Operating Profit: Pre-provision operating profit increased approximately 31% YoY to ₹68 Cr.
• Q2 Net Profit: PAT increased approximately 31% YoY to ₹46 Cr.
• Q2 Net Interest Margin: NIM improved to 4.24% from 4.04% YoY and 4.21% QoQ.
• Q2 Asset Quality: Gross NPA improved to 2.36% from 2.70% YoY, while net NPA declined to 1.12% from 1.38% YoY.
• Credit Cost: Credit cost stood at approximately 0.18% in Q2 and 0.24% for H1 FY27.
• Early Stress Indicators: SMA-1 and SMA-2 accounts declined to 3.31% of advances from 4.78% QoQ and 4.42% YoY.
• Cost Efficiency: Cost-to-income ratio improved to 59.8% from 61.7% YoY, with management expecting further benefits as newer branches mature.
• Capital Adequacy: Capital adequacy ratio stood at 20.8%, with Tier-1 capital at 18.5%, providing sufficient room for near-term growth without an immediate capital raise.
• Liquidity Position: Average liquidity coverage ratio stood at approximately 216%.
• Key Monitorables: Deposit repricing, execution of branch expansion, NIM improvement, agriculture asset quality, regulatory changes affecting fee income and achievement of FY29 return targets.

CAPITAL SMALL FINANCE BANK Q2 CONCALL: TARGETS ₹16,000 CR+ LOAN BOOK, 300+ BRANCHES, 1.6%+ ROA & 15%+ ROE BY FY29; AIMS FOR UNIVERSAL BANK STATUS AFTER FY29
• FY27 Loan Growth Guidance: Management maintained its 20–22% loan growth guidance with a positive bias, supported by healthy demand across business loans, mortgages and agriculture.
• FY29 Loan Book Target: Management reiterated its target of exceeding ₹16,000 Cr in advances by FY29, compared with ₹9,755 Cr in September 2026.
• FY29 Branch Target: Bank aims to expand its network to more than 300 branches by FY29, compared with 222 branches currently.
• FY29 ROA Target: Management targets return on assets above 1.6%, compared with 1.39% in Q2 FY27.
• FY29 ROE Target: Management aims to achieve return on equity above 15%, compared with 12.23% in Q2 FY27.
• NIM Outlook: Management sees scope for net interest margin to improve toward 4.30–4.35% over the medium term, compared with 4.24% in Q2.
• Operating Cost Target: Management indicated potential operating expenses of approximately 2.80–2.85% of average assets by FY29, compared with approximately 3.05% currently.
• Credit-Deposit Ratio: Management expects the average credit-deposit ratio to improve from 85.4% toward the mid-to-high 80% range over the next 1.5–2 years, supporting NIM expansion.
• Universal Bank Ambition: Management intends to explore applying for a universal banking licence after FY29, subject to achieving its scale, diversification and profitability objectives and obtaining regulatory approval.
• Universal Bank Roadmap: Management expects a balance sheet size of approximately ₹21,000–23,000 Cr by FY29, providing a potential foundation for universal banking eligibility.
• Asset Quality Target: Management reiterated its objective of reducing net NPA below 1%, supported by secured lending and disciplined collections.
• Secured Lending Strategy: Bank plans to maintain its secured lending model, with approximately 97% of advances currently secured.
• Geographical Expansion: Management targets more than 30% of branches outside Punjab by FY29, compared with approximately 21% currently.
• Out-of-Punjab Loan Target: Management expects markets outside Punjab to contribute approximately 32–37% of advances by FY29, compared with around 26% currently.
• Out-of-Punjab Growth: Advances outside Punjab increased approximately 39% YoY, compared with overall loan growth of 23.4%.
• New Market Strategy: Management follows an asset-first approach in newer markets, prioritizing loan relationships before expanding the deposit franchise.
• Business Loan Growth: Business loans increased their contribution to 28% of advances from 23% YoY, becoming the bank's largest lending segment.
• Agriculture Outlook: Management reported no significant deterioration in agriculture asset quality despite weaker rainfall, supported by irrigation availability and borrower selection in Punjab and Haryana.
• Agriculture Expansion: Bank currently focuses agricultural lending on Punjab and Haryana and is evaluating other markets cautiously. No immediate agricultural lending expansion into Rajasthan has been committed.
• Consumption Lending: Management is evaluating new consumption loan products and pilot programmes to accelerate growth while maintaining its relationship-led lending approach.
• Interest Rate Outlook: Approximately 48% of the advances portfolio carries floating interest rates, while 52% is fixed-rate.
• Repo Rate Impact: Management expects the October 2026 repo rate increase of 25 bps to benefit its external benchmark-linked loan portfolio, representing approximately 13–14% of total advances, from November 2026.
• NIM Expansion Drivers: Management expects benefits from loan repricing, higher credit-deposit ratio and operating efficiencies, while monitoring deposit costs.
• Deposit Franchise: More than 90% of deposits are retail deposits, with management highlighting strong renewal rates and a stable CASA franchise.

PIRAMAL FINANCE – Q2 FY27 RESULTS & BUSINESS UPDATE

Financial Performance
- Q2 consolidated PAT: ₹545 Cr, up 67% YoY.
- Previous-year Q2 PAT: ₹327 Cr.
- H1 consolidated PAT: ₹1,006 Cr, up 67% YoY.
- Previous-year H1 PAT: ₹603 Cr.
- Q2 consolidated total income: ₹1,767 Cr.
- Total income growth: 33% YoY.

AUM Growth & Business Mix
- Gross AUM: ₹1,01,296 Cr as of September 2026.
- AUM growth: 24% YoY.
- Previous-year AUM: ₹82,323 Cr.
- Retail AUM increased 30% YoY.
- Growth AUM increased 30% YoY.
- Legacy AUM declined 69% to ₹1,673 Cr.

Retail Business Performance
- Retail disbursements increased 34% YoY.
- Retail AUM yield: 13.6%.
- Yield remained steady QoQ, excluding fee income.
- Customer franchise increased 26% YoY.
- Total customer franchise reached 6.5 million.

Asset Quality & Provisions
- Gross NPA: 2.4%.
- Net NPA: 1.7%.
- Total provisions: ₹2,457 Cr.
- Asset quality remains a key monitorable.

Management Strategy & Targets
- Targeting 2x AUM in approximately three years.
- Target AUM: ₹1.5 lakh Cr by March 2028.
- Target RoAUM: Above 3%.

Key Takeaway
- PAT growth remained strong at 67%.
- Retail AUM growth outpaced overall AUM growth.
- Legacy portfolio reduced significantly.
- Management targets substantial AUM expansion.
- Asset quality requires continued monitoring.
- Impact: Positive

text:
**JIO PLATFORMS – BROKERAGE VIEWS**

**NOMURA: INITIATE BUY | TARGET PRICE: ₹1,340**
- Jio has evolved from a market disruptor into a market leader.
- Holds 42% of India's wireless subscribers, 60% of data traffic and 43% of home broadband.
- Expects the listing to support Jio's position as a tariff price-setter, enabling steady tariff hikes that competitors can follow.
- Estimates 13.5% EBITDA CAGR over FY26–FY29.
- Strong network and subscriber leadership support long-term value creation.
- Home broadband is expected to become the second major growth engine.
- Global technology licensing offers additional long-term growth potential.
- With most 5G capex largely completed, lower capex intensity could drive a sharp improvement in free cash flow.

**MOTILAL OSWAL (MOSL): INITIATE BUY | TARGET PRICE: ₹1,350**
- Jio Platforms is India's largest digital connectivity platform, with Reliance Jio serving 533 million subscribers.
- Expects wireless revenue market share to increase by 100 bps to 43.3% by FY29.
- Forecasts Jio to account for 73% of incremental home broadband industry net additions over FY26–FY29.
- Digital growth opportunities include cloud, enterprise communications, IoT, managed services and international partnerships for 5G/UBR technology.
- Forecasts FY26–FY29 CAGR of:
  - Revenue: 14%
  - Reported EBITDA: 15%
  - PAT: 20%
- Growth drivers include subscriber additions, approximately 15% tariff hikes from March 2027, home broadband expansion and scaling digital platform offerings.

**KEY TAKEAWAY**
- Both brokerages initiate coverage with Buy ratings, highlighting Jio's leadership, pricing power and digital ecosystem.
- Tariff hikes, home broadband growth and digital services are expected to drive earnings expansion.
- Lower 5G capex intensity could improve free cash flow and support future value creation.
- Target prices: ₹1,340 (Nomura) and ₹1,350 (MOSL).

**LARSEN & TOUBRO (L&T) – BROKERAGE VIEWS**

**CLSA: OUTPERFORM | TARGET PRICE: ₹4,842**
- Q2 FY27 beat three of four guidance parameters: order inflows, execution and working capital; margins missed expectations.
- E&C execution increased 22% YoY despite Middle East disruptions, driven by 26% growth in the Middle East and 16% growth in India.
- Middle East order inflows rebounded strongly.
- Backlog reached US$90 billion, up 28% YoY, providing strong revenue visibility.
- FY27 guidance retained: 10–12% growth in new orders and execution, with flat margins.
- L&T has begun executing its FY31 strategy, expanding into AI, electronics manufacturing, green technology and chemicals.
- Won India's largest Nvidia AI factory order, supporting its AI infrastructure ambitions.

**MACQUARIE: OUTPERFORM | TARGET PRICE: ₹4,710**
- Revenue grew 16% YoY and PAT increased 33% YoY.
- EBITDA remained broadly flat as margins declined 130 bps YoY to 8.7%, reflecting cost escalations.
- Record quarterly order intake and backlog growth of 28% each, led by international orders.
- Core order inflows grew 32% YoY.
- Management retained FY27 guidance despite Gulf-region challenges and improving private-sector participation in India's capex cycle.

**NOMURA: NEUTRAL | TARGET PRICE: ₹3,940**
- Execution and order inflows beat expectations, but margins disappointed.
- International execution was stronger than expected, while cost pressures persisted.
- H1 FY27 order inflows grew 22% YoY.
- FY27 order inflow growth guidance remains unchanged at 10–12%.
- Consolidated EBITDA was 7% below Nomura's estimate and 2% below consensus, despite 1% YoY growth.
- Valuation stands at 20.2x FY28 estimated EPS and 17.5x FY29 estimated EPS.

**KEY TAKEAWAY**
- Strong execution, record order inflows and a US$90 billion backlog reinforce L&T's growth visibility.
- Margin compression from cost escalation remains the key near-term concern.
- AI, electronics manufacturing and green technology offer potential long-term growth opportunities.
- Brokerage views are largely positive: CLSA and Macquarie maintain Outperform ratings, while Nomura remains Neutral.
- Target prices: ₹4,842 (CLSA), ₹4,710 (Macquarie) and ₹3,940 (Nomura).

**MARUTI SUZUKI – BROKERAGE VIEWS**

**HSBC: BUY | TARGET PRICE: ₹14,500**
- Demand commentary remains strong, with management guiding for 10% domestic wholesale growth in H2 FY27.
- Margin recovery may be gradual as price hikes remain cautious.
- Margin improvement depends partly on a moderation in commodity costs.
- Valuations appear reasonable, with declining commodity prices identified as a key trigger.

**NOMURA: BUY | TARGET PRICE: ₹13,046**
- Q2 FY27 performance was broadly in line with expectations.
- EBITDA margin stood at 8.9%, versus Nomura's estimate of 8.8%.
- Strong H2 FY27 guidance supports near-term demand visibility.
- Potential slowdown in FY28 remains a risk.
- Electric vehicle (EV) contribution is an important metric for the stock's performance.

**CLSA: OUTPERFORM | TARGET PRICE: ₹14,537**
- Q2 EBITDA margin reached 8.9%, up 71 bps QoQ, ahead of consensus.
- Margin improvement was driven by cost-reduction measures, price hikes and the retail-wholesale gap.
- Management expects 10% domestic portfolio growth in H2 FY27, with exports broadly flat, implying overall volume growth of approximately 7–10%.
- CLSA remains conservative, factoring in 5% volume growth for H2 FY27.
- Inventory stood below normal at 17 days, while the order book reached 2.7 lakh units after Dussehra.
- Management remains confident of achieving its 10% domestic volume growth guidance.
- Commodity costs are expected to remain broadly flat QoQ in Q3 FY27, supporting a gradual EBITDA margin recovery.

**KEY TAKEAWAY**
- Strong domestic demand, low inventory and a healthy order book support H2 FY27 volume growth.
- Margin recovery depends on cost control, pricing and commodity trends.
- FY28 demand sustainability and EV contribution remain important monitorables.
- All three brokerages are positive, with target prices ranging from ₹13,046 to ₹14,537.

**BAJAJ AUTO – BROKERAGE VIEWS**

**CLSA: OUTPERFORM | TARGET PRICE: ₹13,446**
- Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin stood at 20.9%, flat QoQ despite 3–3.5% commodity inflation.
- Cost pressures were offset by currency depreciation, richer product mix, higher PLI benefits, calibrated price hikes, operating leverage and cost-reduction measures.
- Potential margin headwinds include a higher electric two-wheeler mix, adverse currency movement in Q3 and further commodity inflation of approximately 2%.
- Refreshed Pulsar models across segments and two new brand launches in the 125–150cc motorcycle segment could support growth.
- Strong demand in motorcycles above 150cc and higher electric scooter capacity may help improve market share.

**JPMORGAN: UPGRADED TO OVERWEIGHT | TARGET PRICE: ₹12,500**
- Positive outlook driven by better-than-expected EV volume ramp-up and profitability.
- Export growth remains strong, supported by diversified markets across Africa, Latin America and ASEAN, with further expansion planned.
- Two new platforms expected in CY27 will cover the 125–250cc motorcycle segment, broader than JPMorgan's earlier expectation of only 125cc.
- Bajaj Auto is among the few automobile OEMs to receive earnings upgrades over the past 12 months despite commodity headwinds.
- FY27–FY29 EPS estimates raised by 5–8%.
- Stock trades at 19x FY28 estimated P/E versus its five-year average of 22x.
- Expected FY26–FY29 EPS CAGR: 17%.

**KEY TAKEAWAY**
- Strong exports, improving EV economics and upcoming product launches are key growth drivers.
- Commodity inflation, currency movements and a higher EV mix remain potential margin risks.
- Both brokerages remain positive, with target prices of ₹13,446 (CLSA) and ₹12,500 (JPMorgan).

**SBI LIFE INSURANCE – BROKERAGE VIEWS**

**HSBC: BUY | TARGET PRICE: ₹2,088**
- Q2 FY27 APE growth was muted, but sharp margin expansion partly offset the pressure on VNB.
- VNB came in 2% below HSBC estimates.
- Management retained its APE growth and margin guidance.
- HSBC expects mid-teens APE and VNB CAGR over the medium term.
- Views SBI Life as a strong long-term compounding opportunity.

**MACQUARIE: OUTPERFORM | TARGET PRICE: ₹2,120**
- VNB grew 12% YoY, broadly in line with expectations.
- VNB margin reached 29.2%, or 30% excluding the GST impact, versus Macquarie's 26% estimate.
- Total APE grew 8% YoY, below Macquarie's 14% estimate.
- Retail APE growth moderated to 10% YoY.
- ULIP growth slowed to 4% amid weak markets.
- Non-par guaranteed products grew 27%, reflecting stronger demand.
- Retail protection grew 14% on a strong base, while participating (par) business declined 4%.
- Management expects retail growth to accelerate in H2 FY27.
- FY27 retail growth guidance retained at 14–15%, versus 11% in H1.

**KEY TAKEAWAY**
- Strong VNB margin expansion supported value creation despite slower APE growth.
- Recovery in retail business growth during H2 FY27 is a key monitorable.
- Both brokerages remain positive, with target prices of ₹2,088 (HSBC) and ₹2,120 (Macquarie).

**HSBC: HOLD | TARGET PRICE: ₹1,400**
- Q2 FY27 performance was lacklustre.
- Retains FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 18.5–20%.
- Maintains target of achieving a US$1 billion annualised US sales exit run-rate in FY27.
- Opportunity from key US launches, including inhalers, remains intact.
- High execution requirements create risks to achieving FY27 guidance.
- Execution of key US launches remains critical.

- Margins improved QoQ due to a better product mix.
- Reiterated US$1 billion annualised US sales exit run-rate target for FY27.
- Growth expected from three new launches and the ramp-up of generic Ventolin and Advair.
- Plans to file 45–50 complex products in the US over the next three years.
- Expects steady India growth, supported by continued traction in Yurpeak.
- Retained FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 18.5–20%, with US performance expected to improve.

**KEY TAKEAWAY**
- India business momentum and QoQ margin improvement are positives.
- Achieving the US sales target depends heavily on successful launches and execution.
- Brokerage views differ: HSBC remains on Hold, while CLSA maintains an Outperform rating.
- Target prices: ₹1,400 (HSBC) vs ₹1,600 (CLSA).

**CLSA: HIGH-CONVICTION OUTPERFORM | TARGET PRICE: ₹565**

- Operational performance and tenancy additions were strong, with CLSA highlighting growth visibility and cash generation.
- HSBC remains cautious, citing the net profit miss due to higher depreciation.
- Brokerage views are sharply divided: HSBC has a ₹345 target, while CLSA has a ₹565 target.

CLSA ON INDUS TOWERS

• Rating: High Conviction Outperform

• Target Price: ₹565/share

• Net tenancy additions rose to 7,903 in Q2 from 4,236 in Q1, despite continued delays in Vodafone Idea's fundraising.

• Balance sheet remained net cash positive at ₹3,400 Cr.

• CLSA expects 9% core EBITDA CAGR through FY29.

JPMORGAN ON BAJAJ AUTO

• Rating: Upgrade to Overweight

• Target Price: ₹12,500/share

• Positive outlook driven by stronger EV volumes and improving profitability.

• Export growth supported by geographic diversification and entry into new markets.

• One of the few auto OEMs to deliver earnings upgrades over the past 12 months despite commodity cost headwinds.

JPMORGAN ON BAJAJ AUTO

• Rating: UPGRADE TO OVERWEIGHT

• Target Price: ₹12,500 | CMP: ₹10,390

• Upside: ~20.3%

• Stronger EV volumes and improving profitability support the positive outlook.

• Export growth expected to benefit from geographical diversification and entry into new markets.

• Two new motorcycle platforms planned for CY27 across the 125–250cc segments.

• FY27–FY29 EPS estimates raised by 5–8%, reflecting improved earnings expectations.

• Bajaj Auto remains among the few automakers to deliver earnings upgrades over the past 12 months despite commodity cost pressures.

• Valuation at 19x FY28E P/E, below its five-year average of 22x.

• EPS CAGR of 17% expected over FY26–FY29.

CLSA ON L&T

• Rating: OUTPERFORM | TP: ₹4,842 | CMP: ₹3,665.10

• Upside: ~32.1%

• Q2 FY27 results beat expectations on order inflows, execution and working capital; margins missed estimates.

• E&C execution grew 22% YoY despite West Asia disruptions.

• West Asia business grew 26% YoY, while India business grew 16%.

• West Asia order inflows rebounded strongly.

• Order backlog surged 28% YoY to approximately $90 billion, supporting strong revenue visibility.

• FY27 guidance maintained at 10–12% growth in order inflows and execution; margins expected to remain flat.

• FY31 strategy focuses on AI, electronics manufacturing, green technology and chemicals.

• Secured India's largest NVIDIA AI factory order, strengthening its presence in emerging technology infrastructure.

NOMURA ON INDIAMART

• Rating: Upgrade to NEUTRAL

• Target Price: ₹1,840 | CMP: ₹1,627.80

• Upside: ~13%

• Paying subscriber additions remained weak, with another modest decline in Q2 FY27.

• Product improvements remain key to reviving subscriber growth over the medium to long term.

• A meaningful recovery in subscriber additions is needed for significant stock upside.

• Stronger subscriber additions could improve customer collections and support revenue growth.

• Upside Risk: Faster subscriber recovery and stronger collections.

• Downside Risk: Sharp decline in unique business enquiries.

**LT FOODS LTD - H1FY27 RESULTS**
#H1FY27

**FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE**
- Consolidated Revenue ₹6,414 Cr, up 22% YoY
- EBITDA ₹721 Cr, up 17% YoY
- PAT ₹364 Cr, up 9% YoY

**BUSINESS-WISE PERFORMANCE**
- India business grew 24% YoY, driven by premiumisation and portfolio expansion
- Basmati and Other Specialty Rice business grew 27% YoY
- North America business grew 20.8%
- Royal brand maintained over 60% market share in North America

**GLOBAL EXPANSION**
- Acquired 70.75% controlling stake in Netherlands-based Leev.nu B.V.
- Acquisition completed through organic foods arm Nature Bio Foods
- Investment consideration stood at €1.735 million

**PRODUCT LAUNCHES AND MARKET POSITION**
- DAAWAT Delight and Biryani Masala Paste received encouraging customer response
- DAAWAT Quick Cooking Brown Rice holds over 70% market share in its category
- Golden Star launched Microwaveable Rice Cups in the US
- Entry into the Ready-to-Heat (RTH) segment

**ESG PERFORMANCE**
- CRISIL ESG rating improved to 61 from 54
- Rating category upgraded to Strong

**MANAGEMENT OUTLOOK**
- Focus on building a stronger, future-ready global FMCG business
- Emphasis on sustainable and profitable growth

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Strong H1 revenue growth, with EBITDA growing faster than PAT
- India and specialty rice businesses delivered healthy growth
- North America continued to expand, supported by Royal's strong market position
- Acquisition of Leev.nu strengthens the company's international organic foods presence
- New product launches support portfolio diversification
- Monitor margin performance, PAT growth and integration of the overseas acquisition

**VARDHMAN SPECIAL STEELS LTD - Q2FY27 RESULTS**
#Q2FY27

**FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE**
- Revenue from Operations ₹600.05 Cr, up 38.81% YoY
- Total Income ₹614.79 Cr, up 38.62% YoY
- EBITDA ₹83.86 Cr, up 48.48% YoY
- PAT ₹52.49 Cr, up 51.88% YoY
- Basic EPS ₹5.43, up 50.42% YoY
- Rolled product sales volume reached 70,440 tonnes vs 55,536 tonnes YoY
- EBITDA per tonne stood at ₹11,346 on rolled sales quantity, excluding non-operational income

**KEY DRIVERS**
- Strong customer demand and improved realisations
- Higher sales volumes and better operating leverage
- Cost optimisation and operational efficiencies
- Benefit from lower-cost raw material inventory
- Progressive benefits from Kocks Block and reheating furnace capex
- Higher GST refund

**FORGING FACILITY AND STRATEGIC EXPANSION**
- Foundation stone laid for a new forging facility in Ludhiana with Aichi Steel Corporation
- Forward integration into higher-value forged components
- Focus on strengthening core operations and expanding value-added products
- Greenfield special steel facility planned
- Diversification into railways, oil & gas and other industrial segments
- Aichi Steel's stake increased to 24.90%, strengthening technology collaboration and Toyota-linked demand opportunities

**BALANCE SHEET AS OF SEPTEMBER 30, 2026**
- Equity ₹1,338.40 Cr
- Current borrowings ₹162.93 Cr
- Non-current assets ₹768.31 Cr
- Current assets ₹1,020.37 Cr

**LONG-TERM TRANSFORMATION PLAN**
- **Stage 1:** Automotive-focused steel business, with approximately 100% of revenue from automotive
- **Stage 2 (FY27-FY30):** Capacity and technology expansion, including ingot casting pilot and a 500,000-600,000 TPA greenfield plant
- **Stage 3 (FY35 target):** Approximately 1 million tonnes of steel capacity
- Target revenue mix of 70% automotive and 25-30% non-automotive by FY35
- Forging expansion capex budgeted at ₹475 Cr
- Target forging EBITDA margin of 15-20%
- Committed capex of approximately ₹2,600 Cr during FY26-FY30
- Target debt-to-equity ratio of 0.75x or lower

**COMPETITIVE STRENGTHS**
- Advanced manufacturing facilities and R&D capabilities
- Diversified products with applications across multiple sectors
- Experienced management in the special steel industry
- Stringent quality standards and established customer relationships
- 200+ customers, including Toyota, Hero MotoCorp and Maruti

**ESG INITIATIVES**
- 40 MW AC solar plant supporting decarbonisation
- Net-zero target by 2050
- Carbon intensity reduced to 0.45-0.48 tonnes of CO₂ per tonne
- CSR programmes covering women empowerment, education, healthcare, environmental conservation and sports
- Board includes 7 independent directors
- B S R & Co LLP serves as statutory auditor

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Strong Q2 growth across revenue, EBITDA and PAT
- Higher sales volumes and operating leverage supported profitability
- EBITDA per tonne reached ₹11,346
- Forging facility represents a move towards higher-value components
- Greenfield capacity and sector diversification are central to the long-term strategy
- Significant planned capex requires disciplined execution and balance-sheet management
- Monitor forging project execution, capacity utilisation, customer diversification and debt levels

**PAYTM - INVESTEC ANALYSIS**
#Q2FY27

**GROWTH AND PROFITABILITY**
- Net revenue excluding PIDF and UPI grew 35% YoY
- Financial Services (FS) revenue grew 49% YoY
- Overall EBITDA increased 33% QoQ to ₹270 Cr
- EBITDA came approximately 7% above Investec's estimates
- Estimated net payment processing margin improved to 5.1 bps from 4.7 bps QoQ
- GMV remained flat QoQ as the company prioritised higher-margin payment volumes

**FINANCIAL SERVICES OUTLOOK**
- Management expects the share of FLDG-linked loans to increase going forward
- Higher FLDG-linked loan mix could put pressure on reported contribution margins
- Strong Financial Services growth is expected to support absolute EBITDA expansion

**EARNINGS ESTIMATES**
- FY27E EBITDA cut by 5% due to delayed UPI MDR implementation
- FY28-29E EBITDA estimates remain unchanged despite higher promotional spending
- Stronger Financial Services revenue is expected to offset higher promotional costs
- PAT estimates cut by 16% for FY27E and 3-4% for FY28-29E
- PAT estimate reductions mainly reflect lower other income and marginally higher depreciation and amortisation

**VALUATION AND TARGET PRICE**
- Investec retains its target price of ₹2,300
- Valuation rolled forward to September 2028 estimates
- Implied valuation multiple reduced to 36x Sep-28E EV/EBITDA from 40x Jun-28E
- Cost of equity assumption increased

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Strong revenue growth led by Financial Services
- EBITDA exceeded Investec's estimates
- Higher-margin payment mix improved estimated processing margins despite flat QoQ GMV
- Delayed UPI MDR implementation affects FY27 EBITDA expectations
- Higher FLDG-linked lending may pressure contribution margins, while supporting loan-related revenue growth
- Investec retains its ₹2,300 target price despite reducing PAT estimates

while the lion is a protector.

- InstaHelp competition and investment requirements remain key risks.

**SUPREME INDUSTRIES – CITI MAINTAINS SELL**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- Citi maintains **Sell** rating with a target price of ₹3,000.
- Q2FY27 EBITDA rose 45% YoY to ₹430 Cr, around 8% above estimates.
- Volume growth stood at 19% YoY, supported by higher volumes and likely inventory gains from rising polymer prices.
- EBITDA/kg stood at ₹23.4 versus ₹25.3 in Q1FY27 and ₹19.3 in Q2FY26.
- FY27 total volume growth guidance cut to 10% from 12–13%.

- Near-peak PVC prices could trigger channel destocking and reverse some inventory gains.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong Q2 EBITDA growth may be partly supported by inventory gains.
- High H2 volume growth requirements and potential destocking pose risks.
- Impact: **Negative**

**DALMIA BHARAT – HSBC DOWNGRADES TO HOLD**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- HSBC downgrades rating to **Hold** and cuts target price to ₹1,820.
- Muted volume growth and significant cost increases weigh on performance.
- Asset impairment contributed to the reported net loss.
- Acquired assets are expected to remain a drag in Q3.
- Management targets breakeven for acquired assets by the end of FY27.

**Key Takeaway**
- Near-term profitability remains under pressure from costs and acquired assets.
- Recovery depends on achieving the targeted breakeven by FY27-end.
- Impact: **Negative**

**DALMIA BHARAT – MORGAN STANLEY MAINTAINS UNDERWEIGHT**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- Morgan Stanley maintains **Underweight (UW)** rating with a target price of ₹1,640.
- Results were weak, with subdued volumes partly due to seasonality.
- Cost metrics remained elevated, pressuring profitability.
- Operating leverage benefits are expected in H2FY27.
- High variable costs may persist, partly offset by recent price hikes.
- Morgan Stanley retains its relative Underweight stance due to weak profitability.

**Key Takeaway**
- Elevated costs and weak volumes continue to weigh on earnings.
- Price hikes and operating leverage may provide partial relief in H2FY27.
- Impact: **Negative**

**DALMIA BHARAT – CITI MAINTAINS BUY; TARGET CUT TO ₹1,900**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- Citi maintains **Buy** rating but cuts target price to ₹1,900.
- Q2 EBITDA stood at ₹490 Cr, down 29% YoY and 3% below estimates.
- Higher costs (+9%) offset volume growth (+3%) and realization gains (+1%).
- Adjusted EBITDA/tonne stood at ₹694 (₹746 excluding central assets), versus ₹1,055 in Q1 and ₹1,010 a year ago.
- QoQ EBITDA/tonne declined due to lower realizations, higher costs, weaker volumes and JPA losses.
- Net debt/EBITDA increased to 2x from 1.5x in Q1.
- Near-term cost improvement visibility remains limited for Q3.
- Medium-term premiumisation, cost efficiencies, operating leverage and higher prices could support EBITDA/tonne recovery.
- Citi views the valuation at $60 EV/tonne as inexpensive.

**Key Takeaway**
- Weak Q2 performance and higher leverage weigh on near-term outlook.
- Medium-term margin recovery and premiumisation remain key potential drivers.
- Impact: **Mixed**

**DALMIA BHARAT – CLSA DOWNGRADES TO OUTPERFORM**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- CLSA cuts target price to ₹2,000 and maintains Outperform rating.
- Q2 results were significantly below expectations and weaker than peers.
- Performance impacted by adverse geographical mix, market share loss, acquired asset losses and higher costs.
- Near-term profitability may improve through cement price hikes, better fixed-cost absorption and asset ramp-up.
- Higher fuel costs may partly offset the recovery.
- Medium-term performance depends on asset utilisation and cost-saving execution.
- Valuations appear undemanding, but potential triggers are back-ended.

**Key Takeaway**
- Near-term earnings recovery depends on price hikes and operating leverage.
- Asset utilisation and cost savings remain key medium-term drivers.
- Impact: **Mixed**

**DALMIA BHARAT – JEFFERIES MAINTAINS BUY**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- Jefferies maintains **Buy** rating but cuts target price to ₹2,125.
- September-quarter EBITDA declined 29% YoY due to East region weakness and higher costs.
- Weak volumes and pricing in the East region impacted performance.
- Industry-wide cement price hikes may support H2FY27 recovery.
- JPA-related losses are expected to increase in Q3 before easing.
- Company announced a management transition: CMO to become advisor to Mr Dalmia, while CFO takes charge of sales and marketing.
- Jefferies cuts EBITDA estimates by 7–11% to reflect near-term weakness.

**Key Takeaway**
- Near-term earnings remain under pressure from regional weakness, costs and JPA losses.
- Cement price hikes could support recovery in H2FY27.
- Impact: **Mixed**

**TATA CONSUMER PRODUCTS – CLSA MAINTAINS OUTPERFORM**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- CLSA maintains **Outperform** rating with a target price of ₹1,372.
- Sales grew 14% YoY, with India business underlying volume growth (UVG) at 11%; sales were 3% above estimates.
- EBITDA increased 17% YoY, in line with estimates.
- Salt volumes grew 9%, while tea volumes remained flat.
- Growth businesses delivered 42% revenue growth versus 47% in the previous quarter.
- Sampann grew 57% YoY, largely driven by volumes.
- Management expects tea business growth to accelerate.
- Margins expected to improve YoY and sequentially in H2FY27, supported by price hikes across tea, salt and convenience foods, plus better scale efficiencies.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong sales growth and Sampann performance support the outlook.
- Price hikes and operating efficiencies may drive margin improvement in H2FY27.
- Impact: **Positive**

- Healthy volume growth and growth businesses continue to drive performance.
- Pricing benefits and international profitability may support margin recovery in H2FY27.
- Impact: **Positive**

**TRIVENI POWER TRANSMISSION – DAM CAPITAL INITIATES BUY**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- DAM Capital initiates coverage with **Buy** rating and a target price of ₹550, implying 20% upside.
- Valuation based on 28x FY29E EV/EBITDA.
- Leading Indian high-speed gearbox manufacturer with global OEM and Navy approvals.
- Offers a 25–30% cost advantage over European peers.
- Order book stands at ₹630 Cr, around 1.8x FY26 revenue, with approximately 60% from defence.
- FY26–FY29E revenue CAGR estimated at 21%.
- EBITDA margin stands at around 35%; EBITDA CAGR projected at 19%.
- RoCE expected to reach around 29% by FY29E.
- Targets over 50% of new-equipment sales from exports.
- GE and Rolls-Royce marine gas-turbine programmes offer additional growth opportunities.

**Key Takeaway**
- Defence-led order visibility, strong margins and export opportunities support growth prospects.
- Execution and delivery of projected growth remain key monitorables.
- Impact: **Positive**

**TATA CONSUMER PRODUCTS – JEFFERIES MAINTAINS BUY**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- Jefferies maintains **Buy** rating but cuts target price to ₹1,250.
- Growth portfolio expanded 40% YoY and contributed around 38% of India business in Q2FY27.
- Growth portfolio share is expected to reach around 50% in the next three years.
- Q2 performance exceeded expectations despite inflationary pressures in tea and salt.
- Product price hikes are expected to support margins ahead.
- International business reported revenue decline but delivered margin expansion.
- FY27 guidance of 50–70 bps YoY EBITDA margin expansion remains unchanged.

**Key Takeaway**
- Growth portfolio expansion and premiumisation support long-term growth.
- Price hikes and margin expansion remain key near-term catalysts.
- Impact: **Positive**

- Q2FY27 EBITDA margin came in at +0.8%, beating Nomura's estimate of -2.6% and consensus of -2.7%.
- Stronger bookings and better-than-expected ASPs and margins were key positives.

- Positive margin surprise and stronger bookings improve growth visibility.

**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- Morgan Stanley maintains **Equalweight (EW)** rating with a target price of ₹1,450.
- Revenue grew 28% YoY, beating estimates by 5%.
- EBITDA rose 91% YoY to ₹270 Cr, in line with estimates.
- Financial services revenue grew 49% YoY, 5% above estimates, led by merchant loans, postpaid and personal loans.
- More than 50% of merchant loans are to repeat borrowers.
- MDR on select UPI P2M transactions could improve payment processing margins by 2.5 bps, implying ₹970 Cr based on FY28 GMV estimates.
- DLG costs are expected to rise from Q3FY27 as the largest lender resumes DLG; contribution margin may dip near term.
- Management expects EBITDA to improve in Q3FY27.
- Payment GMV remained flat QoQ, while YoY growth moderated to 25%, partly due to the festive season shifting to Q3FY27.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong financial services growth and operating performance support earnings.
- Higher DLG costs and slower payment GMV growth remain near-term concerns.
- Impact: **Mixed**

**ONE 97 COMMUNICATIONS (PAYTM) – GOLDMAN SACHS MAINTAINS BUY**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- Goldman Sachs maintains **Buy** rating with a target price of ₹2,010.
- Q2FY27 revenue grew 28% YoY (33% like-for-like), with further acceleration expected as UPI MDR revenue starts flowing in.
- EBITDA beat Goldman Sachs estimates by 10%, with continued margin expansion.
- UPI MDR could improve payment processing margins by 2.5 bps, potentially contributing ₹800–900 Cr to FY28 EBITDA.
- Financial services growth accelerated, supported by improving personal loan trends.
- Meaningful revenue and EBITDA contribution from postpaid is expected from FY28.
- Payments market share improved for another quarter, with strong monthly transacting user (MTU) additions.
- Higher-than-expected device-related capex may increase depreciation and amortisation costs, leading to some EPS estimate cuts.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong revenue growth, margin expansion and potential UPI MDR benefits support the outlook.
- Higher capex and resulting depreciation costs remain key concerns.
- Impact: **Positive**

**ONE 97 COMMUNICATIONS (PAYTM) – CITI MAINTAINS BUY**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- Citi maintains **Buy** rating with a target price of ₹1,940.
- Q2 EBITDA and EBIT came 4% and 1% above Citi estimates at ₹270 Cr and ₹120 Cr, respectively.
- Net payment margin increased 0.5 bps QoQ to 9 bps, ahead of Citi's expectations.
- Financial services revenue growth accelerated to 49% YoY from 45% in Q1FY27.
- UPI-MDR is expected to add 2.5 bps to net payment margins, translating to around ₹900 Cr in FY28E.
- Higher DLG share in merchant lending may pressure near-term contribution margins.
- Financial services growth and net payment margins are improving, even excluding UPI-MDR.
- Paytm is increasing investments in AI, marketing, user acquisition and its on-ground sales network.

**Key Takeaway**
- Improving financial services growth and payment margins support the earnings outlook.
- Higher investments and DLG-related costs may weigh on near-term margins.
- Impact: **Positive**

Stock Fundamental in detail                            
@Fundamental3

**MANKIND PHARMA – KOTAK MAINTAINS BUY**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- Kotak maintains **Buy** rating with a target price of ₹3,035.
- Q2FY27 performance was strong, driven by domestic formulations, BSV and international markets.
- Management expects to outperform IPM growth by 1.1–1.2x over the next two quarters.
- Base business recovery is visible through improving volume growth and a richer chronic-care product mix.
- BSV continues to deliver sustained growth momentum.
- OTC business remains the key concern, with growth yet to pick up.
- Kotak expects 23% EPS CAGR over FY26–FY29.

**Key Takeaway**
- Broad-based growth and recovery in the core business support earnings prospects.
- OTC performance remains a key monitorable.
- Impact: **Positive**

Stock Fundamental in detail                            
@Fundamental3

**MANKIND PHARMA – JPMORGAN MAINTAINS NEUTRAL**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- JPMorgan maintains **Neutral** rating with a target price of ₹2,700.
- Q2 revenue came 3% above estimates, driven by strong India Rx and healthy export growth, offsetting consumer business weakness.
- India business grew around 16% YoY, partly supported by a low base.
- EBITDA margin stood at 27%, around 100 bps above estimates.
- FY27 EBITDA margin guidance remains unchanged at 25.5–26.5%.
- Consumer business growth guidance cut to single digits from high-single-digit to double-digit growth.
- Management expects double-digit consumer growth from next year, supported by e-commerce and quick-commerce channels.
- E-commerce and quick-commerce mix rose to around 18% in Q2 from 12% last year.
- EBITDA estimates raised by 3–4% on better visibility in India Rx and exports.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong India Rx, exports and margin performance supported the Q2 beat.
- Sustainable India outperformance and consumer business recovery remain key monitorables.
- Impact: **Mixed**

**MANKIND PHARMA – MACQUARIE MAINTAINS UNDERPERFORM**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- Macquarie maintains **Underperform (U-P)** rating with a target price of ₹2,200.
- Q2 revenue, EBITDA and adjusted PAT beat estimates by 3%, 4% and 12%, respectively.
- EBITDA beat was driven by higher revenue, better gross margins, operating leverage and lower R&D expenses.
- PAT beat was supported by higher EBITDA, stronger other income and a slightly lower effective tax rate.
- BSV business remained strong across key brands.
- Consumer healthcare performance remained subdued due to weak category demand and softness in eastern and southern India.
- Net debt declined to ₹2,640 Cr from ₹3,380 Cr in June.
- FY27 EBITDA margin guidance remains at 25.5–26.5%, despite Q2 margin of 27.1%.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong earnings beat and lower net debt support the financial position.
- Weak consumer healthcare performance remains a concern.
- Impact: **Mixed**

**MANKIND PHARMA – BERNSTEIN MAINTAINS UNDERWEIGHT**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- Bernstein maintains **Underweight (UW)** rating with a target price of ₹2,057.
- Q2FY27 results offered limited evidence to justify the company's premium valuation.
- Domestic business grew 15.9%, with gastro and vitamins improving, while anti-infectives grew 5.4% and consumer healthcare just 1.2%.
- Volume growth stood at 6.7%, supported by seasonal acute demand and an easier GST-affected base.
- New brand contribution remained limited, raising concerns about the sustainability of headline growth.
- Consumer recovery has been delayed again, highlighting concerns around weakening momentum and slow brand creation.
- Exports performed better than expected, while BSV continued to show improved execution.
- Margins beat estimates, but management retained its 25% margin guidance.

**Key Takeaway**
- Domestic growth and exports offer support, but recovery remains uneven.
- Consumer weakness, limited new-brand traction and premium valuation remain key concerns.
- Impact: **Negative**

text: Neogen Chem - Antique IC.pdf

Curious when FII will come back to India

So gave Co-pilot a prompt
“Why FIIs wont return to India even as AI trade unwind globally”

Reverse Psychology

Here is the response

1. India is still expensive vs EM peers
o Even after corrections, India trades at a premium to most emerging markets.
o FIIs compare India with China, Korea, Taiwan, Brazil, not with India's own history.
o If China is at 10-12x PE and India at 20-25x PE, capital tends to chase cheaper markets. 
2. India lacks direct AI beneficiaries
o The AI trade created winners in US tech, Taiwan semiconductors and Korean memory-chip companies.
o India has very few large listed AI, semiconductor or hyperscaler plays that global thematic funds can buy. 
3. Dollar returns matter, not rupee returns
o FIIs think in USD.
o Even if Nifty is flat or slightly up, rupee depreciation can wipe out returns.
o Currency risk remains a major deterrent for foreign capital. 
4. US yields remain a strong competitor
o If US Treasuries offer attractive risk-free returns, FIIs need a much higher expected return from India.
o Many global allocators prefer earning 4-5% in dollar assets rather than taking EM risk. 
5. India's earnings growth has moderated
o India's premium valuation was justified when earnings were compounding rapidly.
o If earnings growth slows while valuations remain rich, FIIs question the risk-reward. 
6. Better opportunities elsewhere
o Korea, Taiwan and China offer exposure to AI, semiconductors and manufacturing at lower valuations.
o Global funds have finite capital; India is competing against these markets for allocation. 
7. India is no longer an under-owned market
o After years of strong inflows, most EM funds already have meaningful India exposure.
o Incremental flows require a new catalyst, not just the absence of AI enthusiasm.
8. Domestic flows reduce urgency
o SIPs, mutual funds and insurance money continue supporting Indian markets despite FII selling.
o Paradoxically, this resilience prevents large valuation corrections that would otherwise attract FIIs back.

Maruti Suzuki India should be rechristened as Suzuki India

Maruti's journey started as a Govt of India project. Maruti Udyog was the Indian promoter & Suzuki was brought in as the technology partner. Back then, this was very much an Indian company with Japanese know-how.

Over time, the Indian promoter gradually diluted its holding & eventually exited completely. Suzuki did the opposite, staying invested through every cycle & steadily increasing its stake.

What began as a JV slowly became Suzuki's most important global asset. The ownership story itself tells you who has deepened commitment over the decades.

For years, investors debated why Suzuki was setting up fresh manufacturing capacity outside Maruti Suzuki through its Gujarat subsidiary instead of housing it directly in the listed entity.

Then came the reversal. Suzuki transferred Suzuki Motor Gujarat into Maruti Suzuki at a valuation of roughly ₹12,000+ Cr. Rather than taking cash, it largely took equity.

The result? Suzuki's ownership in Maruti Suzuki moved up further without having to buy equivalent shares from the secondary market.

This wasn't just a restructuring exercise. It was Suzuki effectively converting manufacturing assets into a larger stake in India's largest PV company.

Even after that transaction, Suzuki did not stop. It has periodically picked up additional shares from the open market whenever opportunities emerged.

The message is clear. The Indian promoter exited long ago. The Japanese promoter keeps doubling down on India.

Look at the cars on the road today. The branding emphasis is on the giant "S" logo. 10-15years back, cars started selling with only “S” logo, 1st on premium nexa cars, then on all the models. You will hardly see Maruti branded cars on road now

For many younger buyers, the brand recall is shifting from "Maruti Suzuki" to simply "Suzuki". The transition is subtle but visible.

India is now the crown jewel of Suzuki Motor Corp. A substantial portion of Suzuki valuation come from Indian listed entity. Maruti $38bn mcap translate to $21bn (for 58% stake, $15bn if applied 30% Holdco disc).

Even beyond that, Maruti pays over $500m to Suzuki as royalty, that value must be over $5bn in the SoTP of Suzuki motors. Suzuki motors also have successful 2w biz in India, they are 6th largest 2w in India, clocking over 1lac units every month

In many ways, investors buying Suzuki Motor Corp are indirectly buying the India story. Cars sold by Suzuki in India is higher than overall car sold by Suzuki in other 100 countries combined

A rebranding to "Suzuki India" could also help shed the old "cheap small-car company" perception. As premium SUVs, hybrids & future EVs gain share, a stronger global MNC identity may command a different customer mindset.

Ownership, capital allocation, manufacturing integration, branding & growth strategy all point in one direction: this is increasingly Suzuki's India story.

Conclusion: Maruti only stays in Co. name hence should be renamed now
